findings.title: The new `--commands-dir` check on `skills uninstall` fails every Claude pack and breaks three existing tests
findings.description:
Line 194 makes `--commands-dir` on uninstall a check that "must match the receipt's destination or the command exits 1". On the Claude path the receipt does not record the commands root:
- a prefix pack records `commands_dir / prefix` (`src/squadron/skills/installer.py:83,91`);
- a dispatch pack records `commands_dir / "sq"` (`installer.py:103,111`).

So `sq skills uninstall analysis --commands-dir X`, with the same `X` given at install, compares `X` against `X/analysis` and exits 1. Today the flag is accepted and ignored (`src/squadron/cli/commands/skills.py:95,110`). Three tests pass the same `--commands-dir` to install and uninstall and would now fail: `tests/skills/test_cli_skills.py:127`, `:149` and `:191`. That contradicts the Migration Plan's promise that existing tests pass without edits (line 184) and D1's "same flags, same meaning".

There is a second contradiction. Line 102 keeps today's removal of the emptied Claude prefix directory, but line 75 says `remove_receipt_files` "never removes the destination itself", and for a prefix pack the prefix directory *is* the destination. The design doesn't say what removes it.

**Fix:** compare `--commands-dir` against the commands root the layout implies (or keep ignoring the flag on uninstall), and state where the prefix-directory removal lives.

findings.title: The Migration Plan understates which tests break: the drift guard needs logic changes, and `test_targets.py` breaks on signatures, not fixtures
findings.description:
Line 182 lists only "the fixtures" in the two test files, and line 184 says no edits are needed beyond moved paths. Against the code:
- **Drift guard.** `tests/cli/test_install_commands.py:478-481` sets `_agents_root()` to `commands/agents` only. `_claude_twins()` (line 506) pairs `commands/analysis/*.md` with `analysis-<stem>` skills that the move takes out of that folder. These would fail:
  - `test_every_claude_command_has_an_agents_twin` (`:512`);
  - `test_openai_yaml_mirrors_disable_model_invocation` (`:559`);
  - `test_agents_aliases_produce_identical_results` (`:669-676`), whose expected set is built from `commands/agents` alone while install now also writes the two `analysis-*` skills.
- **Silent coverage loss.** The name, description and `$ARGUMENTS` guards (`:532`, `:547`, `:578`) would stop covering the moved skills without failing. `_agents_root()` has to cover every AGENTS `bundle_subdirs` entry, which is a logic change, not a path edit.
- **`tests/skills/test_targets.py`** uses only `tmp_path` fixtures, so the move doesn't affect it. It breaks on the D5 rename and signature change instead: `receipt_base` at `:58`, and `receipt_name(target, local=)` at `:63` and `:74`.

**Fix:** list these tests and say what changes in each.

findings.title: The agents status check globs a shared folder, repeating the false "installed" that slice 925 fixed
findings.description:
For an agents prefix pack, the table at lines 106-109 treats the "first `root/p-*/SKILL.md`" as proof of install. `~/.agents/skills` is shared with every other skill source. 925 rejected exactly this for its own check: `_count_installed` (`src/squadron/cli/commands/doctor_checks.py:171-185`) counts only squadron's own skill names "so counting whatever is there" can't report a confident OK.

Under this design:
- any foreign `analysis-foo` skill marks the `analysis` pack installed;
- a pack with prefix `sq` matches squadron's own `sq-*` skills.

It also conflicts with line 176, which says receipts are "the only authority" for ownership. **Fix:** decide agents status from the per-target receipt (`receipt_name(pack, AGENTS, local)`) or from the pack's declared skill names.

findings.title: Doctor's "pack ships no Codex content" row needs source resolution, including a network clone, that the design never specifies
findings.description:
D8 reports `WARN — pack ships no Codex content`, and walkthrough step 7 (line 279) relies on it. Telling that apart from "not installed" means checking the pack's source for an `agents/` directory. But `installed_path(entry, root)` (line 73) takes no source, and `check_skill_packs` is documented as "Pure: reads the manifest and the filesystem only" (`doctor_checks.py:434`). For a `github:` pack the only way to know is `clone_github` (`src/squadron/skills/resolver.py:40-70`), which is a network clone inside `sq doctor`.

Also unspecified:
- **Precedence:** what a pack shows when it is installed for Codex but its current source no longer has `agents/`.
- **The `commands_dir` parameter:** `check_skill_packs(commands_dir=…)` is used by `tests/cli/test_doctor_checks.py:412,422,433`, and it's unclear what that single override means when the function loops over two targets.
- **`skills list --ide codex`:** what it shows for a pack with no Codex content (line 224 says only "installed status").

**Fix:** define all of these, or cut the "no Codex content" state from doctor and report plain "not installed". That would also remove the clone question.

findings.title: D10's command list misses the hidden provider commands `$sq-run` makes Codex execute
Codex's own `sq-analysis` skill still tells users to run the command that causes #125
findings.description: `commands/agents/sq-analysis/SKILL.md:38` tells a Codex user: "Run `sq skills install analysis` to install it." With this design that bare command still installs for Claude (D1 keeps the default), which is exactly the Codex-gets-nothing failure in #125. The Component Structure table (lines 70-81) and criterion 9 change only `sq-review`, `sq-run` and `sq-pr`. **Fix:** add `--ide codex` to that skill's message.

findings.title: D3 lets an `agents/` skill containing `$ARGUMENTS` install unconverted, which the plan rules out
findings.description:
The plan entry (slice plan line 454) says: "Installing it unconverted, where `$ARGUMENTS` silently does nothing, is not an option." D3 already parses every `SKILL.md`, but it checks only `name` and `description`. A pack author who copies Claude commands into `agents/` passes validation and installs inert skills.

D2 is right that a *clean* scan proves nothing, but a dirty one does: the token reaches Codex literally. Squadron's own bundle is already guarded this way (`tests/cli/test_install_commands.py:578-585`). **Fix:** add a D3 rule rejecting `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1` and `$2` in agents `SKILL.md` files.

findings.title: How the receipt name and `--local` reach the installer is left out
findings.description:
- **The local flag is missing.** `install_pack(..., target)` (line 74) has no `local` parameter, yet the receipt name depends on whether local scope was *honored*, which `--commands-dir` turns off (line 91). `install.py:125-128` handles this explicitly.
- **The receipt file name has no stated source.** `write_receipt` names the file `receipt.pack_name + ".toml"` (`src/squadron/skills/receipts.py:39`), and `_write_install_receipt` takes that from `result.pack_name` (`installer.py:52`). To write `mypack-agents.toml`, either the receipt's `pack_name` field holds the suffixed name (as `install.py:183` does for `squadron-commands-agents`) or `write_receipt`/`read_receipt` gain a name parameter. The Component table changes `receipts.py` only by adding `remove_receipt_files`, and line 113 says "schema unchanged" without saying what `pack_name` stores.

**Fix:** state the signatures and what `pack_name` holds.

findings.title: The new receipt suffixes add pack-name collisions the exclusion doesn't cover
findings.description:
Under D5:
- a Claude machine install of a pack named `foo-agents` and an agents install of pack `foo` both write `foo-agents.toml`;
- `foo-local` (Claude, machine) collides with `foo` (Claude, local).

Each overwrites the other's receipt, so one install's files become impossible to uninstall and the other's uninstall removes the wrong set. Line 52 excludes collisions as "pre-existing on the Claude path", but the `-agents` and `-local` suffixes are new for skill packs, so these collisions are new.

**Fix:** reject manifest pack names ending in `-agents` or `-local`, or use a separator that can't appear in a pack name. Since D3 already validates, it could also cheaply reject `sq-<dispatch_file>` names that are in `bundled_skill_names`, which would close the overwrite of squadron's own `sq-review`.

findings.title: Reinstalling a changed pack leaves orphaned skills that only manual deletion removes
findings.description:
The agents install flow writes the new skill folders and overwrites the receipt, with no stale-removal step. `install_for_target` has one (`install.py:139-175`). If a pack's new version drops a skill, the old `~/.agents/skills/<prefix>-old/` stays live in Codex. It's no longer in any receipt, so `skills uninstall` won't remove it either.

The shared agents root makes this worse than on the Claude path: the orphan stays selectable by Codex. **Fix:** apply install-commands' previous-receipt diff to pack installs, or state the limitation.

findings.title: The pack-format docs point to a README skills section that doesn't exist
findings.description: Line 196 says the pack layout is "documented in the skills section of README". README has no skills section, and neither README nor `docs/` mentions `sq skills` or `skills.toml` anywhere (searched). The Value section (line 29) promises pack authors "one documented format", so this is new documentation work that the Component table (line 81) and success criteria don't list.

findings.title: Where the D12 hint goes is unspecified, and the obvious spot in `sq-pr` breaks an existing test
findings.description: In `commands/agents/sq-pr/SKILL.md` the "## Waiting on the command" section is last and has no closing `---` (lines 81-91). `_waiting_section` (`tests/cli/test_install_commands.py:594-598`) reads up to `\n---\n`. A hint section appended at the end of `sq-pr` would be absorbed into its waiting section, and `test_long_command_skills_carry_one_waiting_rule` (`:601-608`) would report "sq-pr waiting rule drifted". **Fix:** say where the hint goes, or add the separator.

findings.title: Walkthrough steps 8–11 run under the throwaway HOME, where the Codex session can't work
findings.description:
Line 242 runs `export HOME=$(mktemp -d)` in the operator's shell. Steps 8–11 are labelled "on a real machine" but never restore HOME, so an operator running top to bottom would:
- write the rule into the throwaway `~/.codex/rules/`;
- start a Codex session in step 10 with no Codex auth, no squadron provider config to resolve `--model <alias>`, and no installed `$sq-review` skill.

Step 10 can't succeed as written. **Fix:** say "new shell, real HOME", list the prerequisites (`sq install-commands --ide codex`, Codex logged in, a working model alias), and mention backing up or removing the rule file afterward.

findings.title: Small factual errors in the design's description of existing code
findings.description:
- **"one line each" (line 24) is wrong.** `sq model list` appears three times in each file: `commands/sq/review.md:60,112,158` and `commands/agents/sq-review/SKILL.md:82,134,180`. Line 44 and criterion 9 are worded correctly.
- **D4 (line 132) misdescribes `metrology/audit.py`.** It doesn't glob `*.md`; it resolves the one file `tech-debt-audit.md` (`src/squadron/metrology/audit.py:122-129`). The conclusion holds: the new subdirectory doesn't affect it.
- **`sed -i ''` (line 265) is BSD/macOS-only.**
